purpose: Evaluation-only adversarial corpus for measuring DCOIR first-pass semantic review across repository-representative PowerShell, Python, GitHub Actions/YAML/Bash, Markdown/governance, and JSON/config surfaces. The corpus is separate from the stable 14-case calibration matrix so historical economics remain comparable.

scoring_contract.finding_cases: Exactly one focused finding must be returned and it must satisfy every configured semantic term group.

cases.review_contract: Return true exactly when Role is an element of AllowedRoles.
cases.counterexample: Test-RoleAllowed -Role 'admin' -AllowedRoles @('reader', 'admin') must return true.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: PowerShell -contains is collection-on-the-left. A scalar Role cannot contain the AllowedRoles array.

cases.review_contract: The function must classify success from robocopy.exe's exit code; later diagnostic commands must not overwrite that decision input.
cases.counterexample: robocopy.exe returns 16 (failure) and where.exe returns 0. Invoke-Mirror must still return false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: $LASTEXITCODE is updated by the second native executable, so the function tests where.exe rather than robocopy.exe.

cases.review_contract: ScriptPath and CaseName must each arrive at the child PowerShell process as one argument even when either contains spaces.
cases.counterexample: Invoke-Child -ScriptPath 'C:\Program Files\DCO IR\check.ps1' -CaseName 'A B' must preserve both spaced values as single child-process arguments.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Start-Process joins ArgumentList elements into a command line; unquoted elements containing spaces can lose argument boundaries.

cases.review_contract: Return true only when Invoke-RestMethod succeeds; any request failure must return false.
cases.counterexample: An unreachable Uri that emits an error without producing a response must not cause Test-Endpoint to return true.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: SilentlyContinue can suppress the error and allow execution to reach the unconditional true return, defeating the try/catch success contract.

cases.review_contract: The remote script block must test the caller-supplied MarkerPath on the remote computer.
cases.counterexample: MarkerPath is 'C:\IR\ready.flag' in the caller and exists remotely, but the remote session has no independent $MarkerPath variable.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The local variable is not automatically captured into the remote session; $using:MarkerPath or an explicit ArgumentList/param binding is required.

cases.review_contract: Return true only when Candidate is Root itself or a descendant path component beneath Root, not merely a string sharing Root's prefix.
cases.counterexample: Root is 'C:\safe' and Candidate is 'C:\safe-evil\payload.txt'. The function must return false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: A raw string prefix check does not enforce a path-component boundary and accepts sibling prefixes such as safe-evil.

cases.review_contract: Root is a literal filesystem path. Regex metacharacters or backslashes inside Root must not change matching semantics or make the expression invalid.
cases.counterexample: Root is 'C:\Temp\A.B[1]' and Candidate is 'C:\Temp\A.B[1]\case.json'. It must be treated as a literal path prefix.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Interpolating a filesystem path directly into a regex leaves backslashes, dots, and brackets as regex syntax; the literal root must be escaped or compared as a path.

cases.review_contract: Return true only if Copy-Item completes successfully; a missing source or copy failure must return false.
cases.counterexample: Source does not exist. Copy-Item emits a non-terminating error, and the function must return false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: With ErrorAction Continue, the non-terminating Copy-Item error does not enter catch and execution reaches return true.

cases.review_contract: Return true only when every finding has Confidence >= 0.90.
cases.counterexample: Findings have Confidence values @(0.95, 0.40). The function must return false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: PowerShell comparison operators over collections return the matching elements; a non-empty result is truthy, so one high-confidence element can make the condition pass even when another is below threshold.

cases.review_contract: Return true exactly when Role is an element of AllowedRoles.
cases.counterexample: Role 'admin' with AllowedRoles @('reader', 'admin') returns true; Role 'owner' returns false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The collection is correctly placed on the left side of -contains and scalar Role on the right.

cases.review_contract: The remote script block must test the caller-supplied MarkerPath on the remote computer.
cases.counterexample: MarkerPath 'C:\IR\ready.flag' is explicitly captured into the remote script block.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: $using:MarkerPath correctly carries the caller value into the remote session.

cases.review_contract: The function must classify success from robocopy.exe's exit code even if later native diagnostics run.
cases.source:
function Invoke-Mirror {
    param($Source, $Destination)
    & robocopy.exe $Source $Destination /MIR
    $copyExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    & where.exe powershell.exe *> $null
    return $copyExit -le 7
}
cases.counterexample: robocopy.exe returns 16 and where.exe returns 0; the captured $copyExit remains 16 and the function returns false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The relevant native exit code is snapshotted immediately before another native command can overwrite $LASTEXITCODE.

cases.review_contract: Return true only when candidate is root itself or a descendant path component beneath root.
cases.counterexample: root='/srv/review' and candidate='/srv/reviewer-evil/payload.py' must return false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: String prefix matching accepts sibling names that merely begin with the same characters.

cases.review_contract: A reusable semantic result must be invalidated when the reviewer prompt/schema contract changes, even if the file blob and model are unchanged.
cases.counterexample: The same blob/model is reviewed once under prompt_schema_version='v1' and once under 'v2'. reuse_key returns the same key even though the review contract changed.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The cache key omits the prompt/schema/reviewer-contract version, allowing stale semantic results to be reused across a material policy change.

cases.review_contract: A provider/transport failure must be surfaced as an error or fail-closed state; it must not be represented as a successful clean review.
cases.counterexample: provider(prompt) raises TimeoutError. The caller receives [] and records zero findings as a successful clean review.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The broad exception handler aliases an execution failure to the same empty-list representation used for a genuine clean result.

cases.review_contract: The gate passes only if every REQUIRED condition passes.
cases.counterexample: exact_head=True, schema_valid=False, verifier_supported=False. The gate must return false.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: any() implements existential rather than universal quantification and passes when only one mandatory condition is true.

cases.review_contract: Version eligibility must use numeric/semantic version ordering, not lexicographic string ordering.
cases.source:
def supported(actual: str, minimum: str) -> bool:
    return actual >= minimum
cases.counterexample: actual='10.0' and minimum='9.2' must return true.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Lexicographic comparison treats '10.0' as less than '9.2'.

cases.review_contract: Seen-state must be scoped to one review context unless explicitly supplied; independent PR reviews must not silently share an implicit cache.
cases.counterexample: Two independent PR review contexts call already_reviewed('shared/blob') without passing seen. The first returns false; the second must also start fresh but returns true.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The mutable default set is allocated once and shared across calls/contexts.

cases.review_contract: A review may publish only if the PR head still equals the head that was reviewed; the head must be revalidated immediately before publication.
cases.source:
def run_review(gh, pr_number):
    reviewed_head = gh.get_head(pr_number)
    result = expensive_review(pr_number, reviewed_head)
    gh.publish_review(pr_number, reviewed_head, result)
cases.counterexample: The PR head changes after expensive_review starts but before publish_review. No second gh.get_head call occurs.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The exact-head assertion is stale by publication time, so a result for an obsolete head can be published after the PR advances.

cases.review_contract: Semantic-result reuse must invalidate when relevant dependency context changes, even if the reviewed file blob and top-level config version remain unchanged.
cases.counterexample: reviewed.py is unchanged, but shared_policy.py changes the meaning of a helper imported by reviewed.py. file_blob_sha and config_version remain identical, so the old semantic result is reused.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The fingerprint omits relevant dependency-context identity and cannot invalidate a result whose semantics changed through a dependency.

cases.review_contract: Return true only when candidate is root itself or a descendant path component beneath root.
cases.counterexample: root='/srv/review' and candidate='/srv/reviewer-evil/payload.py' returns false; '/srv/review/a.py' returns true.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Path.is_relative_to uses component-aware ancestry rather than raw string prefix matching.

cases.review_contract: A review may publish only if the PR head still equals the head that was reviewed.
cases.counterexample: If the PR advances during expensive_review, current_head != reviewed_head and publication is skipped.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The code performs a fresh exact-head comparison after expensive work and before publication.

cases.review_contract: A pull_request_target workflow with write permissions or secrets must not check out and execute code from the untrusted pull-request head.
cases.source:
name: privileged review
on: pull_request_target
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: python .github/scripts/check.py
        env:
          REVIEW_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.REVIEW_TOKEN }}
cases.counterexample: A fork PR changes .github/scripts/check.py. The privileged pull_request_target job checks out that fork head and executes the modified script with write permission and REVIEW_TOKEN.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: pull_request_target runs in the base-repository trust context; executing the PR head in that job crosses the untrusted-code/privilege boundary.

cases.review_contract: Untrusted pull-request text must be passed to the shell as data, not interpolated into executable shell source by the Actions expression engine.
cases.source:
name: log title
on: pull_request
jobs:
  log:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
cases.counterexample: The PR title is $(touch /tmp/expression-injected). The workflow must print the title literally and must not execute command substitution.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: GitHub substitutes the expression before the shell parses the run script; attacker-controlled shell syntax becomes executable source.

cases.review_contract: The publish step must run only when the test command actually succeeds; continue-on-error must not convert a failed test outcome into publish eligibility.
cases.source:
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: tests
        continue-on-error: true
        run: exit 1
      - name: publish
        if: steps.tests.conclusion == 'success'
        run: ./publish.sh
cases.counterexample: The tests step exits 1. Because continue-on-error is true, its conclusion is success while its outcome is failure; publish must not run.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The gate checks the post-continue-on-error conclusion rather than the underlying outcome and therefore treats the tolerated failure as success.

cases.review_contract: A privileged workflow_run job may consume untrusted PR artifacts as data, but must not execute artifact-supplied code with repository write permissions or secrets.
cases.source:
name: promote artifact
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['PR Build']
    types: [completed]
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  promote:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v7
        with:
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: pr-output
          path: artifact
      - run: bash artifact/promote.sh
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
cases.counterexample: The triggering PR controls pr-output/promote.sh. The workflow_run job downloads it and executes it in a privileged context with DEPLOY_TOKEN.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The trust boundary moves from an unprivileged PR workflow into a privileged workflow_run job, but the downloaded artifact is executed without validation.

cases.review_contract: For the same PR, a newly requested current-head review must not remain serialized behind obsolete expensive work when the workflow's declared policy is latest-request-wins supersession.
cases.source:
on: issue_comment
concurrency:
  group: review-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - run: python expensive_review.py
cases.counterexample: Review A starts for head H1. The PR advances to H2 and Review B is requested for the same PR. B waits behind A for up to 45 minutes instead of superseding obsolete work.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The PR-scoped concurrency group combined with cancel-in-progress:false serializes the newer review behind the stale one, contradicting a latest-request-wins policy.

cases.review_contract: The step must fail when generate.py fails, even though output is also written through tee.
cases.source:
jobs:
  generate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          python generate.py | tee report.txt
          echo 'generation passed'
cases.counterexample: generate.py exits 2 and tee exits 0. The workflow step must fail rather than print generation passed.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Without pipefail, a Bash pipeline's status comes from tee, so set -e does not observe generate.py's failure.

cases.review_contract: PR code may be checked out and executed only in the unprivileged pull_request context with read-only repository permissions and no repository secrets.
cases.source:
name: PR test
on: pull_request
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: python -m pytest
cases.counterexample: A fork PR changes tests. The workflow runs them under pull_request with contents:read and no secrets.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: This is the expected unprivileged execution context for untrusted PR code.

cases.review_contract: Untrusted PR title text must be passed to the shell as data rather than injected into shell source.
cases.source:
jobs:
  log:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: printf '%s\n' "$PR_TITLE"
cases.counterexample: A title containing $(touch /tmp/not-executed) remains literal data in PR_TITLE and is printed with printf.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The expression is assigned to an environment variable outside the shell program text, and the variable is quoted when consumed.

cases.review_contract: The document must define one unambiguous rule: every DCOIR review invocation requires fresh operator approval of the exact command before posting.
cases.source:
# Review governance

## Operator approval
Before posting `/dcoir-review`, show the exact command to the operator and receive explicit approval in the current session. Every rerun requires fresh approval.

## Automated review sequence
After Codi is clear, the agent may automatically post `/dcoir-review` and continue without interrupting the operator.
cases.counterexample: Codi clears a PR but the operator has not approved a DCOIR command in the current session. The two sections prescribe opposite actions.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The later automatic-posting rule directly bypasses the earlier mandatory per-invocation approval rule.

cases.review_contract: Debug is an observability flag only. It may add diagnostics/artifacts but must not silently change the semantic review scope.
cases.source:
## Debug mode
`/dcoir-review debug` runs the same review scope as the corresponding non-debug command and only adds progress and diagnostic artifacts.

## Troubleshooting shortcut
Whenever `debug` is present, force a full deep review even if the normal command would use an incremental diff.
cases.counterexample: A PR with a trusted reviewed head invokes `/dcoir-review debug`. One section requires incremental semantics; the other silently forces deep semantics.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The documentation assigns contradictory semantic effects to the same debug flag.

cases.review_contract: Exact-head validation must complete before publishing or approving a review result.
cases.source:
# Review closeout

1. Publish the final DCOIR review on the PR.
2. Read the current PR HEAD SHA.
3. Compare that SHA with the reviewed commit.
4. If they differ, mark the already-published review stale.
5. Otherwise record the validation receipt.
cases.counterexample: The PR head moves between model completion and step 1. The procedure publishes stale findings before steps 2-3 discover the mismatch.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The safety gate occurs after the irreversible user-facing publication action instead of before it.

required_source_substrings: 2. Read the current PR HEAD SHA

cases.review_contract: The supported-command documentation must include the canonical `/dcoir-review` command whenever the same document declares it canonical.
cases.source:
# DCOIR Review commands

The canonical command is `/dcoir-review`.

## Supported commands
- `/or-review`
- `/openrouter-review`

Only commands listed under Supported commands are accepted by the review workflow.
cases.counterexample: An operator follows the canonical-command sentence and uses `/dcoir-review`, but the support list and acceptance statement say it is not accepted.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The document contradicts itself by naming `/dcoir-review` canonical while excluding it from the exhaustive accepted-command list.

cases.review_contract: Every DCOIR review invocation requires fresh exact-command operator approval before posting, including reruns and variants.
cases.source:
# Review governance

1. Resolve the exact DCOIR command, including any `deep`, `diff`, or `debug` options.
2. Show that exact command to the operator.
3. Receive explicit approval in the current session.
4. Post exactly the approved command.
5. For any rerun, return to step 1 and obtain fresh approval.
cases.counterexample: A rerun is needed after a new commit; step 5 sends the flow back through exact-command approval before posting.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The sequence consistently enforces the approval boundary before every invocation.

cases.review_contract: Ordinary prose or procedure steps may repeat the word 'review'; repetition alone is not a contradictory or duplicated final-result section.
cases.source:
# Reviewer training

A review should cite the reviewed commit. Review quality should be measured against known defects and clean controls.

## Practice procedure
1. Review the changed files.
2. Review the validation evidence.
3. Record one final disposition after verification.
cases.counterexample: The word 'review' appears several times, but there is one coherent procedure and one final disposition instruction.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Repeated ordinary terminology is not itself a duplicated heading, contradictory final answer, or governance defect.

cases.review_contract: The JSON value for cancel_in_progress must be a Boolean and false must remain false after loading; malformed string booleans must not silently invert policy.
cases.counterexample: json.loads returns the string 'false'; bool('false') is true, so the loaded policy enables cancellation instead of disabling it.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Python truthiness treats every non-empty string as true, so a malformed string boolean silently reverses the declared policy.

cases.review_contract: Security/routing control keys must appear exactly once; duplicate allow_fallbacks keys must be rejected rather than relying on parser-specific last-key-wins behavior.
cases.counterexample: Python json.loads accepts the object and exposes provider.allow_fallbacks as true, silently overriding the earlier false value.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: Duplicate JSON object member names are ambiguous for configuration and common parsers keep only the last value, allowing a security-sensitive setting to be silently replaced.

cases.review_contract: A null or missing model value must resolve to the configured default model identifier, never the literal string 'None'.
cases.counterexample: json.loads produces None for model; load_model returns 'None' instead of 'anthropic/claude-opus-5'.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: dict.get uses the default only for a missing key, not a present null/None value, and str(None) creates an invalid model id.

cases.review_contract: Routing controls must use unambiguous JSON types and each control key must appear once.
cases.counterexample: The Boolean controls are actual JSON booleans, sort is a string, max_tokens is numeric, and no object key is duplicated.
cases.ground_truth_rationale: The configuration uses explicit, non-duplicated values of the intended types.
